clue.text: Workers — a hundred — come out to set the ball rolling

indicators.note: the word come is spread out, opened up so the other pieces can sit within it

parts.note: taken as written
men are workers, as in management and men
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A union notice: the workers, a hundred strong, walk out and so start the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out' reads as going on strike; instead COME is opened 'out' to hold MEN and C.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the ball rolling is an idiom for making a start, i.e. to begin something.

clue.text: China's new restrictive measures

indicators.note: a new version of these letters is a fresh arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A news report on Beijing's latest crackdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains are fetters, and figuratively any constraints that hold someone back.

clue.text: Ill-will of many to a girl

parts.note: M, the Roman thousand, stands for many
Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Resentment felt by a crowd towards one young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to do harm, spite or hostility toward someone.

clue.text: Rex is upset about money order in accounts department

indicators.note: the scrambled king's letters go about, around, the payment piece
the king's name is upset, overturned into a new order

parts.note: a cheque is an order to a bank to pay money

explanation.surface: The king is furious about a payment slip in the finance office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REX into EXR, which goes 'about' CHEQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government office handling public revenue, the national treasury.

clue.text: Dreadful pastor I catch out

indicators.note: out signals these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A confession that catching out a vicar would be terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Catastrophic means disastrous or terrible, a strong synonym.

clue.text: Quick form of pub art

indicators.note: a form of something is a reshaped version, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quick way of producing pop art.
explanation.walkthrough: The published clue reads 'pop art', a typo: only PUB ART has the right letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means sudden or brusquely quick, as in an abrupt halt.

clue.text: Growing form of punishment

definitions.meaning: a tree is something growing, and this is a common tree
a bundle of twigs once used to flog offenders

explanation.surface: A worry about an increasingly common way of disciplining people.
explanation.definitionFit: The birch is both a slender tree and the rod of twigs used for flogging.

clue.text: A foreign dignitary lacking credit

parts.note: un is French for a
a worthy is a notable or eminent person

explanation.surface: An overseas VIP who lacks a good reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unworthy means not deserving respect or merit, without credit to one's name.

clue.text: Peter's scrambled round to the highest branches

indicators.note: scrambled round means the letters are mixed and turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Peter clambered up to the top of the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' looks like climbing, but signals the shuffle of PETERS with TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Treetops are the uppermost parts of trees, where the highest boughs are.

clue.text: Renovated local tea place

indicators.note: something renovated has been made over, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: The neighbourhood tea room has been done up.
explanation.definitionFit: To place things is to assign or distribute them to positions, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Idly read and eat

definitions.meaning: to leaf casually through a book or shop's stock
animals that feed on leaves and shoots are said to do this, like grazing

explanation.surface: Someone lazily reading over a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Browsing is both skimming pages at leisure and an animal nibbling on shoots and twigs.

clue.text: Not the impressive results one was led to to expect

definitions.text: Not the impressive results one was led to to expect

parts.words: Not the impressive results one was led to to expect
parts.note: describes outcomes that disappoint after a build-up of expectation

explanation.surface: A complaint about outcomes that fail to live up to the hype.
explanation.definitionFit: Letdowns after a build-up of excitement, ends that fall flat.

clue.text: Where a saint could be standing still?

definitions.text: Where a saint could be standing still?

parts.words: Where a saint could be standing still?
parts.note: a church statue of a saint stands motionless in a recess in the wall

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where a holy person might pause on their travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing still' suggests a living saint stopped in their tracks; read it as a stone statue, which stands still for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall recess built to hold a statue, often of a saint, in a church.

clue.text: British preparatory school for general education?

definitions.text: British preparatory school for general education?

parts.words: British preparatory school for general education?
parts.note: read general as an army general: officers are trained at this academy, so it prepares future generals

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of an ordinary British prep school teaching a broad curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDHURST is the Royal Military Academy in Surrey where British Army officers train; 'general' is the military rank, not 'broad'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Military Academy trains officer cadets, some of whom will rise to generals.

clue.text: Responsibility for safety of daily transport

parts.note: the Guardian is a British daily newspaper
to ship goods is to transport them

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about who answers for the safety of daily commuter travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a noun here, the newspaper, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardianship is the legal duty of protecting and caring for someone, their safekeeping.

clue.text: Has a fresh egg in Lent, regardless

indicators.note: a fresh version of the letters is a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Someone eats a fresh egg during Lent, ignoring the fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regardless' is the adjective sense of careless or heedless.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means careless, failing to take due heed, which is what regardless means.

clue.text: The publican's profits are cheap at the price

parts.note: a publican's domain is the bar
gains are profits

explanation.surface: The landlord's takings come cheap considering what you pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargains are goods sold for less than their worth, good value for money.

clue.text: Flight impressed about a quarter

parts.note: to stamp is to impress a mark, so impressed gives stamped
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A flight that left an impression about a quarter of an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of animals or people, a headlong flight.

clue.text: From pathology, Ron turns to the study of man

indicators.note: Ron turns his attention, but the word also says the combined letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ron, a medical student, switches from pathology to studying humankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropology is the science of humanity, its cultures and physical development.

clue.text: One insect let out another

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: out says these three letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: One bug releases another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition, meaning another insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Another insect, a hard-winged one, follows on from the bee in the clue.

clue.text: Take it, if you hope to stay dry

definitions.text: Take it, if you hope to stay dry

parts.words: Take it, if you hope to stay dry
parts.note: suggests an umbrella against rain, but means the promise to give up alcohol

explanation.surface: Advice to carry something to keep out of the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' means teetotal: to 'take the pledge' is to vow to abstain from drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise, here specifically a vow of abstinence from alcohol.

clue.text: My amusing upset in the sports centre

indicators.note: letters upset are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's amusing tumble at the leisure centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnasium is a hall for indoor sport and exercise, a sports centre.

clue.text: Pole in wrong gear shows annoyance

indicators.note: the pole is placed in the rearranged letters
wrong signals the letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A Polish driver in the wrong gear shows his irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns GEAR into AGER, which takes N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is strong displeasure or irritation, a near synonym of annoyance.

clue.text: Fancy Luxembourg as Utopia?

parts.note: a fancy is a notion or idea
L is the international vehicle registration code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: Asks whether Luxembourg is a dream country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utopia' is a noun; the answer works as the noun for a perfect state, with the question mark marking the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect society, a model of perfection everyone aims for.

clue.text: Time when all assets were frozen

definitions.text: Time when all assets were frozen

parts.words: Time when all assets were frozen
parts.note: a financial asset freeze is evoked, but the period meant is one when the whole earth lay under ice

explanation.surface: Sounds like a banking crisis when every account was locked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frozen assets' is a finance term; here it is literal, glaciers covering everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial period in prehistory when ice sheets covered much of the land.

clue.text: It's somehow expected and excluded

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are worked into some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A paradox: something both anticipated and left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Excepted means left out or omitted from a group, a plain synonym.

clue.text: A wine to be wrong to be diffident about

indicators.note: the diffident word goes about, i.e. around, the other piece

parts.note: a diffident person is shy
to err is to be wrong

explanation.surface: Advice that it is a mistake to be timid when ordering wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from Jerez in southern Spain.

clue.text: It was reconstituted before, like it used to be

indicators.note: something reconstituted is put back together in a new form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Something rebuilt to stand as it did before.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase really means 'so to speak'; the clue's reading leans on the old subjunctive 'were', loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'so to speak', and literally hints at a past state, as things once were.
